page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 2696.98, placing it in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is limited due to the 2-vCPU configuration, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with uncached read-only large block bandwidth at 30.8 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 22.14 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2as_v5 offers a low-entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The high memory density per vCPU makes it qualitatively cost-effective for applications requiring moderate compute but substantial memory allocation. However, the lack of local storage and poor database operations performance represent notable tradeoffs. This server is best suited for light memory-optimized workloads, basic text processing, small-scale caching, or development environments requiring a dedicated AMD EPYC processor with 16 GB of RAM.
